Executive Answer

How AbarVa gets smarter without becoming a black box.

AbarVa does not rely on vague model memory. It improves through governed knowledge layers: researched corpus, industry pattern packs, tenant context, client-approved overrides, and audited data loads. Moves and Source use those layers at runtime through brokers, retrieval, validation rules, and citations.

What changes for a client? Sharper decisions, not looser AI.

Every new rate card, modernization pattern, or client file must be parsed, validated, approved, versioned, and cited before it can influence an answer or estimate.

The five knowledge layers

Each layer has a different owner, update path, and trust level. The agent does not treat all text equally. Client-approved context outranks generic research; tenant-specific rate cards outrank benchmark rate cards; unsupported model guesses do not outrank evidence.

Layer What it contains Who can update it How agents use it
Research Spine Official sources, citations, confidence, extraction notes, open gaps. AbarVa research and engineering. Provides benchmark fallback and explains assumptions.
Global Corpus Reusable playbooks, standards, rate-card methods, modernization archetypes. AbarVa release process. Gives Moves and Source a structured operating model.
Industry Pattern Packs Healthcare, retail, airline, banking, and other industry-specific patterns. AbarVa plus expert review. Shapes domain-specific recommendations and evaluation criteria.
Tenant Context Client apps, vendors, systems, contracts, org roles, KPIs, evidence files. Client admins through Data Loads. Grounds answers in the client reality, not generic market advice.
Client Overrides Approved client rate cards, policy choices, mappings, exceptions, preferences. Client stewards and approvers. Overrides generic benchmarks and changes estimates for that tenant only.

How an update becomes available

Whether the update is a rate card, modernization research, a pattern pack, or a client data file, the path is deliberately controlled. The goal is speed with evidence, not uncontrolled training.

1

Register

A template or corpus object defines required fields, formats, owner, cadence, and what it unlocks.

2

Load

Admin uploads through Data Loads with tenant identity and operator attestation.

3

Protect

Files pass sensitive-data, malware, format, tenant, and size controls before parsing.

4

Parse

Deterministic parsers extract rows, facts, evidence, rates, or workload inventory. Formula cells are not trusted.

5

Validate

Required fields, ranges, enums, provenance, confidence, source dates, and tenant boundaries are checked.

6

Commit

Approved data is versioned into the data plane, indexed, and made available through brokered agent tools.

How it integrates into the data plane

Current Pattern

Parse first, commit only after gates pass

Data Loads first creates a validation preview. For context files, approved rows become tenant-scoped chunks/facts and are queued for embedding. For rate cards, the new path validates rows today; the commit table slice will write approved rates as tenant-scoped pricing corpus.

Availability

Brokers make the data usable

Moves and Source do not query random tables directly. A typed broker resolves the right tenant, pulls the approved corpus/context, applies precedence rules, and returns a compact evidence bundle to the agent.

Data type Parsed into Available to Precedence
Rate card Internal loaded-cost rows, vendor/SI bill rates, geo modifiers. Moves estimates, Source pricing normalization, BAFO questions. Client-approved rates over researched benchmark.
Modernization pack Archetypes, disposition rules, automation ranges, effort coefficients. Moves modernization baseline, Source SI scorecard, divergence report. Analyzer inventory over generic industry defaults.
Tenant context Evidence chunks, structured facts, provenance, audit trail. Intelligence, Moves, Source, Tower, Steward. Approved tenant evidence over global corpus.
Research ledger Source IDs, URLs, as-of dates, confidence, extraction status. All agents as provenance and fallback explanation. Official source rows over uncited assumptions.

Detail view: how the pieces come together

The simple version is this: every important update becomes a typed object, every typed object has a parser and validation contract, approved objects are committed with provenance, and the product pages bind to brokered read models. The user sees a calm page; underneath it is a controlled dataflow.

Business workflow What the Maestro experiences
Select template → Upload file → Review findings → Approve → Use in Moves / Source

The page should not expose implementation language. It should say: what was loaded, what failed validation, what needs approval, and which decisions become sharper after approval.

Technical dataflow What the platform does
Next.js route → Tenancy check → Parser → Validator → Data-plane write → Read broker

The write path and read path are deliberately separate. Upload APIs validate and commit. Product pages read through brokers. Agents receive a compact evidence bundle, not raw database access.

Agent grounding flow What the model receives
User question → Surface context → Tenant evidence → Corpus pattern → Rules and citations → Answer

This is runtime grounding. The agent is not asked to remember everything. It is handed the approved facts and rules needed for this client, this page, and this decision.

What is actually inside the corpus?

In plain terms, the corpus is AbarVa's structured business knowledge library. It is not a pile of PDFs and it is not a hidden model brain. It is a set of versioned, reviewed building blocks that tell agents how to reason about a business problem, what evidence to look for, what standards apply, what good looks like, and what questions to ask when the data is incomplete.

Corpus item Plain-English example What it teaches the agent Where it shows up
Pattern "How a healthcare system should modernize Epic/Clarity analytics to a lakehouse." The standard approach, common traps, target architecture, and governance expectations. Moves modernization plan; Source SI evaluation.
Rate-card method "How to compare internal labor cost, SI onshore rates, offshore rates, and geo modifiers." How to calculate planning cost without trusting spreadsheet formulas or vague benchmarks. Moves cost baseline; Source commercial negotiation.
Archetype "A SAS workload with macros is harder than a simple report repoint." How to classify work, estimate complexity, and explain why effort differs. Modernization estimates and SI bid normalization.
Scorecard "Do not pick the lowest-cost SI if architecture, security, or delivery risk is weak." How to evaluate vendors using weighted criteria, not opinion. Source RFP, BAFO, and recommendation summary.
Evidence rule "A claim about vendor spend must cite a contract, invoice, or approved client file." What evidence is acceptable, stale, missing, or low-confidence. Sentinel answers; Steward governance checks.
Prompt discipline "Answer like a CIO advisor, but disclose missing data and do not invent exact numbers." How the agent should communicate, what to refuse, and when to ask for clarification. Sentinel, Nexus, Moves, Source, and Steward.
Corpus example

Modernization pattern pack

  1. Legacy archetypes: DataStage, stored procedures, SAS, marts, Tableau/BO.
  2. Disposition rules: retire, retain, replatform, re-architect.
  3. Standards: Databricks Well-Architected pillars, medallion model, Unity Catalog.
  4. Effort logic: foundation work, framework work, per-workload work.
  5. Questions to ask SIs: automation proof, reconciliation plan, security model, delivery team.
Corpus example

Rate-card pack

  1. Internal loaded-cost method from official wage and benefits sources.
  2. Vendor/SI rate method from public schedules and client-approved quotes.
  3. Geo modifier method for national baseline to local region.
  4. Validation rules: low cannot exceed high, source and as-of date required.
  5. Output rule: always label planning range, confidence, and source.
Corpus example

Source procurement pack

  1. RFP structure and required vendor response sections.
  2. Commercial normalization model: compare bids on equal scope.
  3. Risk flags: vague automation claims, missing transition plan, weak security detail.
  4. BAFO question patterns: ask vendors to close specific evidence gaps.
Corpus example

Hallucination rules

  1. If no tenant evidence exists, say the answer is benchmark-based.
  2. If a value is stale, label it stale.
  3. If a required file is missing, ask for that file.
  4. If the user asks for an exact number, show range and assumptions unless approved data supports exactness.

Examples that make it concrete

These examples show how the same operating model supports a rate-card update, a modernization baseline, and a Source vendor evaluation.

Example 1

Client uploads a rate card

  1. The client selects Internal loaded cost rates or Vendor and SI hourly rates.
  2. The CSV is checked for tenant identity, attestation, sensitive data, and file limits.
  3. The parser normalizes headers like Function Group, Role Level, and Hourly Low USD.
  4. The validator checks ranges, enums, as-of date, confidence, and source.
  5. After approval, the rate rows become the tenant's pricing corpus.
  6. Moves uses those rates before falling back to benchmark rates.
Example 2

Client loads a modernization inventory

  1. The client runs Databricks Lakebridge/Analyzer or supplies a similar inventory export.
  2. AbarVa ingests metadata: platform, artifact type, complexity, LOC/counts, dependencies, and disposition.
  3. Raw code bodies are rejected because AbarVa does not rescan or convert code.
  4. The modernization pack maps each workload to an archetype and effort range.
  5. Moves combines workload effort with the approved rate card to produce a planning baseline.
  6. Source uses the baseline to evaluate SI bids and find divergence.
Example 3

CDAO evaluates three SI bids

  1. AbarVa creates the independent baseline from inventory, archetypes, standards, and rate cards.
  2. Each SI response is normalized to the same scope and scoring dimensions.
  3. Source compares price, architecture fit, automation leverage, security, team model, and timeline.
  4. The divergence report shows where an SI bid is cheaper because it changed scope or assumed easier work.
  5. BAFO questions are generated from the gaps, not generic procurement text.
Example 4

Evidence is missing or stale

  1. The broker cannot find an approved client rate card, current inventory, or required source field.
  2. The page shows an honest empty state or warning, not a fabricated number.
  3. The agent can use a benchmark only if it labels it as benchmark and shows confidence.
  4. The recommended action becomes a data-load or clarification task.

How the Next.js / React page binds to actual data

AbarVa pages should look simple, but they should not be static mockups. The page loads a tenant-scoped read model on the server, passes typed data into React components, and renders clear states: ready, blocked, empty, or degraded.

Server page

Server component resolves tenant and read model

The Next.js page runs on the server. It resolves the active client, calls a broker, and passes only the display-ready model to the React view.

page.tsx resolveActiveClient() → getMovesRateCardReadModel(clientKey) → getModernizationBaseline(clientKey) → <MovesPage model={model} />
React view

Component renders facts, not assumptions

The component does not invent rows. It receives a typed model with values, provenance, warnings, and empty states. If the broker says no live data, the page says no live data.

model.rateCard.status ready → show client rates benchmark → show benchmark label missing → show upload action blocked → show validation findings
Page element Data binding What a CXO sees Failure behavior
Rate-card status tile Tenant rate-card broker reads approved rows and source ledger. Client-specific, benchmark, or missing. Show upload/approval action, not a fake rate.
Modernization baseline Analyzer inventory broker + archetype coefficients + approved rate card. Planning range by workstream and disposition. Show planning assumptions and missing inventory gaps.
Source scorecard SI response parser + weighted scorecard + baseline comparison. Why one bid is stronger, weaker, cheaper, or riskier. Block final recommendation if required SI fields are missing.
Agent answer panel Brokered evidence bundle, corpus pattern, user question, permission scope. Answer with citations, confidence, and next action. Ask for clarification or disclose insufficient evidence.

What parsing means, and where the data lives

Parsing means turning an uploaded file into structured, usable, governed data. A spreadsheet, PDF, Analyzer export, or contract is not directly useful to an agent. AbarVa has to identify the file type, extract the right rows or facts, validate them, attach provenance, and store them in the right tenant-scoped data plane so pages and agents can retrieve them safely.

Landing and protection Before parsing
Admin upload → Azure Blob landing zone → Tenant key → Malware / sensitive scan → Quarantine if needed

Raw files should land as tenant-keyed objects first. If the file contains restricted data, malformed content, or suspicious payloads, it is held before any parser or agent can use it.

Parse and validate Turning files into records
CSV / XLSX parser → Document Intelligence → Analyzer parser → Validation rules → Approval queue

Different file types use different parsers. CSV and workbook rows use deterministic row parsers. PDFs and documents can use Azure Document Intelligence for layout/text extraction. Lakebridge-style inventory files use a metadata parser and reject raw code bodies.

Store and index Making data live
Azure/Postgres tables → Audit ledger → Embeddings / search index → Read broker → Pages and agents

Structured rows live in Azure/Postgres data-plane tables. Text evidence can also be chunked and indexed for retrieval. The audit ledger records who loaded it, when it was approved, which parser ran, and what version became active.

Service / layer What it stores or does Why it matters Example
Azure Blob landing zone Raw uploaded files, tenant-keyed and scan-gated. Keeps raw files controlled before parsing or indexing. Rate-card workbook, Analyzer export, PDF contract.
Azure Document Intelligence Extracted document layout, text, tables, and page anchors. Makes PDFs and documents parseable without treating them as magic text blobs. Contract clauses, board report tables, policy documents.
Azure/Postgres data plane Tenant-scoped structured records, inventory rows, rates, facts, run ledgers. Provides the durable system of record for approved data. Vendor rate rows, workload inventory, enterprise context facts.
Embedding / search index Searchable chunks with source locators and freshness metadata. Lets agents retrieve the right evidence quickly without reading every file. "Show me evidence for Apex vendor concentration risk."
Audit ledger Load runs, parser version, validation findings, approvals, commit history. Lets AbarVa replay why an answer or estimate used a source. "Carlos approved Vendor Contracts v3 on June 3."
Typed brokers Read models that enforce tenant, precedence, and evidence rules. Pages and agents get clean facts and states, not raw database access. Moves gets approved rate card; Source gets normalized baseline.
What parsing does

Rate-card CSV

  1. Reads columns like function group, role level, low/high rate, source, and confidence.
  2. Normalizes human headers into canonical fields.
  3. Rejects bad math, missing source, invalid confidence, or low greater than high.
  4. Stores approved rows as tenant pricing data that Moves can use.
What parsing does

Analyzer inventory

  1. Reads metadata about jobs, reports, SQL objects, SAS programs, and dependencies.
  2. Classifies each workload by archetype and complexity.
  3. Rejects raw code bodies because AbarVa is not the conversion tool.
  4. Stores workload metadata for modernization estimates and SI evaluation.

How agents get smarter

The word training can be misleading. AbarVa does not need to fine-tune the base model every time a client uploads a file. The safer model is runtime grounding: each agent is given the right facts, patterns, policies, and examples at the moment it works.

Moves

Smarter estimates and choices

Moves uses rate cards, modernization archetypes, tenant inventory, value logic, and assumptions to produce planning ranges, not unsupported precision.

Source

Smarter vendor evaluation

Source uses the same corpus to normalize SI bids, compare sourcing models, flag divergence, and generate BAFO questions.

Steward

Smarter governance

Steward uses approvals, data quality, tenant isolation, and audit history to decide what the agent is allowed to rely on.

Agent input How it is controlled What the agent must show
Retrieved tenant evidence Tenant-scoped broker, approved-only filters, source locators. Client-specific citations and freshness.
Corpus pattern Versioned release record, source ledger, confidence tags. Pattern source and whether it is benchmark or client-specific.
Client override Approval queue, version history, rollback path. Override label and who approved it.
Missing evidence Validation findings and clarification workflow. Explicit gap, not a guessed answer.

How Sentinel and Nexus use the corpus differently

Think of the corpus as the playbook library. Sentinel is the evidence-grounded analyst. Nexus is the orchestration brain that decides which playbooks, tools, and surfaces should be used for a larger workflow. Both use the corpus, but they use it in different ways.

Agent Role in plain terms Example question How the corpus helps Hallucination control
Sentinel Answers questions using approved client evidence. "What is our biggest modernization risk?" Pulls tenant inventory, modernization pattern, risk rules, and citations. Must cite files or say the evidence is missing.
Nexus Chooses the workflow and coordinates tools. "Build a plan to evaluate three lakehouse SI bids." Selects Source RFP pack, modernization scorecard, rate-card method, and BAFO workflow. Routes to structured tools and approval gates rather than free-form improvisation.
Moves Turns a business move into cost, value, risk, and decision artifacts. "What should this modernization cost?" Combines workload archetypes, rate cards, tenant inventory, and value model. Shows planning range, assumptions, source, and confidence.
Source Helps buy better by structuring vendor decisions. "Which SI bid is most credible?" Uses RFP scorecard, baseline, rate normalization, and divergence patterns. Flags missing vendor evidence and prevents lowest-price-only answers.
Training in layman terms What we do and do not do

We do not "train" the agent by dumping client documents into the model and hoping it remembers them. That would be risky, hard to audit, and hard to update. Instead, we ground the agent at runtime: when the agent answers, AbarVa supplies the exact approved evidence, patterns, rules, and sources relevant to that tenant and task.

Specific example Sentinel answering a CIO
CIO asks risk question → Retrieve app inventory → Apply modernization pattern → Check evidence freshness → Answer with citations

If the application inventory is missing owner fields, Sentinel does not invent owners. It says the risk view is incomplete and asks for the owner-mapping file or steward approval.

Specific example Nexus coordinating Source
CDAO wants SI evaluation → Nexus selects Source workflow → Loads scorecard → Uses rate-card baseline → Produces BAFO questions

Nexus is not making up procurement strategy. It is orchestrating the approved Source playbook, the client's baseline, and the vendor response evidence.

How clients customize patterns

The near-term model is template-driven uploads. The future model is an admin studio where a client can review, edit, approve, version, and simulate overrides before they affect agents.

Now

Template uploads

Clients upload rate cards, context files, mappings, and evidence through governed templates. Bad rows are blocked before commit.

Next

Review and approve

Admins see parsed rows, validation gaps, provenance, confidence, and the exact agent surfaces that will be affected.

Future

Pattern Studio

Clients maintain their own approved patterns: rate cards, sourcing policies, modernization rules, risk weights, and scoring criteria.

Client action Example Control Agent impact
Upload a rate card Internal loaded-cost rates and vendor hourly bands. Parser validation, approval, versioning. Moves estimate uses client rates instead of benchmark.
Override a modernization rule Classify SAS workloads as re-architect, not replatform. Impact preview, approver signoff, rollback. Moves baseline and Source scorecard reflect client policy.
Update RFP weights Increase security from 10% to 20% for healthcare. Governed settings with audit trail. Source ranks SI bids with the client's priority model.
Retire a pattern Mark an old vendor benchmark as stale. Effective date, replacement rule, audit note. Agents stop using stale assumptions.

How hallucination is minimized

Hallucination is reduced by narrowing what the agent is allowed to rely on, making missing data visible, and forcing every important number or claim to carry provenance.

Evidence before assertion

Agent answers must cite tenant evidence, a corpus source, or a benchmark source. If none exists, the answer should say so.

Tenant isolation

Every retrieval and write path is scoped to the active client. Cross-tenant data cannot be used to fill a gap.

Confidence and freshness

Sources carry as-of dates, confidence, and extraction status. Stale or low-confidence evidence is labelled.

Validation before commit

Rates, enums, required fields, ranges, and provenance are checked before data becomes agent-available.

No silent fallback

If a client rate card is missing, the estimate can use a benchmark only if it is clearly labelled as benchmark.

Audit and replay

Data loads, approvals, agent source bundles, and release records make important answers reconstructable.

The board-level answer

AbarVa becomes smarter by expanding controlled knowledge, not by letting the model improvise. Research updates become versioned corpus. Client uploads become validated tenant context. Approved overrides change Moves and Source through brokered retrieval. Every important number must show where it came from, how current it is, whether it is client-specific, and what is still missing.
